original_question: (Well-known problem). Does there exist a finitely presented(infinite) simple group requiring more than two generators? Cf. 6.44 in Archive.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.45 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", explicitly referring back to Archive Problem 6.44. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it asks for a finitely presented, infinite, simple group that is not generated by two elements, and it correctly keeps the cross-reference to Archive Problem 6.44. It is essentially the right target. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
missing_details: Make the existential quantifier explicit by naming the group, e.g. "Does there exist an infinite simple group G ... ?"
Unpack the parenthetical "(infinite)" into the stand-alone condition that G is infinite and simple.
Define "requiring more than two generators" as d(G) > 2, where d(G) is the minimal size of a generating set of G; equivalently, G is not 2-generated.
If you want the paper-faithful context, note that this is the finitely presented strengthening of Archive Problem 6.44, whose finitely generated version is recorded there as solved.
refined_question: Does there exist an infinite simple group G such that G admits a finite presentation and d(G) > 2, where d(G) denotes the minimal number of generators of G?
justification: The exact target is Problem 21.45, which asks whether there exists a finitely presented infinite simple group requiring more than two generators. The only explicit contextual pointer supplied there is "Cf. 6.44 in Archive." Archive Problem 6.44 asks for a finitely generated infinite simple group requiring more than two generators and records that this was achieved by V. S. Guba; therefore 21.45 is specifically the finite-presentation strengthening of that older problem, not a broader neighboring question. The paper gives no further special notation, side hypotheses, or explicit equivalent reformulation near 21.45, so the only implicit detail needed to make the question fully stand-alone is to spell out that "requiring more than two generators" means minimal generator number greater than 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.0300.pdf))
